claims.text: The target materials are as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys.
Their magnetocaloric response is governed by interplay between a first-order magnetostructural transition and deposition-induced microstructure.
Their hysteresis is governed by interplay between a first-order magnetostructural transition and deposition-induced microstructure.
The FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys undergo a first-order magnetostructural transition under the relevant conditions.
Changing laser power and scanning speed can control the alloy microstructure.
Deposition parameters induce changes in grain size.
Deposition parameters induce changes in phase distribution.
Controlled deposition parameters can tailor the magnetocaloric response.
Controlled deposition parameters can tailor hysteresis.
Composition may influence the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis independently of deposition-induced microstructure.
Thermal history may influence the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis independently of deposition-induced microstructure.
The predictions hold only within limits of deposition-parameter ranges and microstructural variation.
A systematic deposition-parameter series with measurements of microstructure, magnetocaloric response, and hysteresis can test the hypothesis.
Failure to observe the predicted outcome together with absence of correlation between microstructure and both magnetocaloric response and hysteresis would falsify the hypothesis.
